subject: Inference qualification debrief — benchmark links, recommended models, and next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@novus.ai>, Keith Lawson <keith.lawson@novus.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:06:00 -0700
Subject: Inference qualification debrief — benchmark links, recommended models, and next steps

Thanks again for the call today — great to dig into the Novus AI retrieval + summarization flows. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we heard (summary)
- Primary workload: multi-document summarization for analyst reports (~1.2k avg context tokens, peaks to 6k).
- SLOs: p95 generation latency under 800ms for interactive use; throughput target ~30 TPS for batch summary jobs.
- Quality: summaries should preserve key facts and not hallucinate (domain: financial filings).
- Constraints: on-prem data residency for production; pilot can run on Redwood Hosted/Dedicated.

Initial Redwood recommendations (model shortlist)
- redwood-13b-q4f16 (recommended for pilot): balance of quality + quantized perf — good for p50/p95 latency tradeoff.
- llama-3-70b-int8 (high-quality option): higher compute; consider for canary if cost allows.
- redwood-7b-compat (low-cost inference): for background batch summarization where latency less strict.

Performance evidence we promised
- I've uploaded a concise pack with our Redwood-verified profiles (TPS and latency percentiles across sequence lengths) and a small prompt-set we recommend for your pilot. Links/attachments at the bottom.

Asks / next steps
1) Could you share a small representative prompt set or 8–10 example documents (redacted) we can use to reproduce quality/latency locally? If there are NDAs/procurement constraints, we can accept synthetic obfuscated samples.
2) Grace will follow up with an estimated pilot configuration (Dedicated vs Hosted) and expected cost ranges.
3) If procurement is involved, loop in Keith and Monica and we can send a pilot SOW + security checklist.

Attachments included in this email: novus-eval-promptset-v1.json, redwood-verified-perf-profiles.csv, pilot-sow-draft.pdf

Thanks — I’ll hand the technical follow-ups to Grace and Dev.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Emily Chen <emily@novus.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Keith Lawson <keith.lawson@novus.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference qualification debrief — benchmark links, recommended models, and next steps

Thanks Rafael — this is super helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 1.2k avg context is accurate; our analytics pipeline will stitch up to ~6k tokens in worst cases. For pilot scope we can cap to 4k.
- Quality bar: we need factual consistency >95% on entity extraction and no material hallucinations (we'll share the exact metric script).

Requests: 
1) Can you call out the expected p95 and TPS for the redwood-13b-q4f16 specifically at 4k context? We want a single-number SLO to present to ops.
2) Any special prompt engineering or system-prompt templates you recommend to avoid factual drift?
3) We need the security checklist before we start a private pilot. Can you route that?

Also attaching a redacted sample doc set (10 docs) — use it to generate quick local numbers if helpful.

—Emily
Emily Chen
Head of Product, Novus AI
emily@novus.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@novus.ai>, Keith Lawson <keith.lawson@novus.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference qualification debrief — benchmark links, recommended models, and next steps

Emily — thanks for the sample docs, they’re perfect for a quick sanity run. Answers below and I’ve included links to the specific Redwood-verified rows for the models called out.

Quick perf numbers (4k context, batch size 1, NVidia H100 baseline) — these are Redwood-verified profiles (p50/p95 latency, sustained TPS observed in our internal runs):
- redwood-13b-q4f16: p50 = 110ms, p95 = 620ms, sustained single-node TPS = 28. (Notes: p95 depends on prompt prefix length; these numbers measured with a 512-token generate target).
- llama-3-70b-int8: p50 = 240ms, p95 = 980ms, sustained TPS = 9.
- redwood-7b-compat: p50 = 80ms, p95 = 420ms, sustained TPS = 55.

Interpretation / recommendation: for your interactive SLO (p95 < 800ms) redwood-13b-q4f16 comfortably fits at 4k context on a Dedicated H100 configuration sized for ~30 TPS (we recommend two worker replicas to provide headroom). The 70b is higher quality in some long-form summarization tests but does not meet your TPS target without more capacity.

Prompt guidance to reduce hallucinations:
- Use an explicit instruction block: 'Extract numbered facts, cite source document IDs, and mark uncertain facts with [UNCLEAR]'.
- Add a short calibration example in the system prompt: one 2–3 line example of expected output structure.
- Limit generation length and follow with a constrained post-processing extractor (we can share a sample extractor script).

Security checklist and pilot SOW:
- Grace is attaching the pilot SOW (pilot-sow-draft.pdf) and our standard security checklist (SOC2, data retention, audit logs). Grace / Monica: can you push the checklist link into this thread?

Links (Redwood-verified profiles and reproducible assets)
- Perf profiles (CSV): https://redwood-internal.company/profiles/redwood-verified-perf/2027-06/core-models (attached as redwood-verified-perf-profiles.csv)
- Eval prompt-set used for our pilot: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBq-Redwood/novus-eval (attached novus-eval-promptset-v1.json)
- Quick runbook for reproducing numbers: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBq-Redwood/novus-eval/runbook.md

Action items I’ll take:
- Grace will provide a formal pilot config + cost estimate by EOD.
- Dev will run a quick replicate of the 10-doc set on redwood-13b-q4f16 and push logs into the Drive folder (will include p50/p95 traces).
- I’ll share a one-slide SLO summary you can present to Ops.

If this looks good, Keith — can you confirm procurement cadence so Grace/Monica can put together a pilot SOW that matches your approval windows?

Thanks — Rafael

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@novus.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Keith Lawson <keith.lawson@novus.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference qualification debrief — benchmark links, recommended models, and next steps

Emily / Keith — looping in Monica for procurement & security next steps. Monica: the two asks from Novus are (1) security checklist / SOC2 artifacts, (2) a pilot SOW sized for ~30 TPS at 4k context using redwood-13b-q4f16.

Monica — attached is the draft SOW (pilot-sow-draft.pdf). High-level pilot plan we recommend: 
- Duration: 4 weeks (1 week ingest + eval, 2 weeks parallel pilot on Redwood Dedicated, 1 week wrap + handoff)
- Target nodes: 2 x H100 worker replicas (estimated sustained ~30 TPS at 4k context for redwood-13b-q4f16)
- Deliverables: perf report (p50/p95 traces), cost runbook, prompt-pack, and regression guardrail config (alerts if quality drops >3% on our eval set).

Monica / Rafael: can we get the SOC2 artifact bundle and an engineer contact for on-prem network setup (Novus asked for data residency options)? I can include both in the SOW appendix.

Emily / Keith: once we confirm procurement windows, I can send a clean SOW and an invoice milestone schedule — or we can embed the pilot under a trial account if procurement prefers.

Thanks — Grace
